purpose: Legal, source-backed research corpus for NSE 200 Momentum 30 Algorithm Prediction. Do not store copyrighted book text or pirated PDFs in this repo.
copyright_rule: Use publisher metadata, public abstracts, legally available papers, and our own derived principles only. No full copyrighted book chapters or copied pages.
project_hypothesis: Nifty200 Momentum 30 should be studied as a rules-based cross-sectional momentum/factor portfolio, not as a daily high-turnover bot. The research priority is point-in-time universe reconstruction, official constituent validation, transaction-cost-aware backtesting, and regime/risk overlays.

sources.title: Algorithmic Trading: Winning Strategies and Their Rationale
sources.author: Ernest P. Chan
project_takeaways: Backtesting and automated execution must be treated as engineering problems, not just strategy ideas.
Mean-reversion, momentum, risk management, and execution costs need separate tests.
A strategy should be rejected if realistic costs, slippage, borrow/margin constraints, or out-of-sample tests destroy it.

sources.title: Time Series Momentum
sources.author: Tobias Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
project_takeaways: Trend-following should be tested across horizons and asset classes, not assumed from one market.
The Momentum 30 engine should compare cross-sectional momentum with time-series trend filters.
Global market trend features may be useful only if tested with strict date availability.

sources.title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency
sources.author: Narasimhan Jegadeesh, Sheridan Titman
project_takeaways: The correct first benchmark for Momentum 30 is intermediate-horizon winner selection, not intraday prediction.
Formation and holding periods must be varied in walk-forward tests.
Post-formation reversal risk should be measured rather than ignored.

sources.title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
sources.author: Clifford Asness, Tobias Moskowitz, Lasse Heje Pedersen
project_takeaways: Momentum can be combined with value/quality diversifiers instead of relying on one crowded signal.
Nifty200 Momentum 30 prediction should track sector/factor crowding and diversification.
Global lead-lag features should be tested as regime features, not treated as guaranteed causal signals.

sources.title: Trading Costs of Asset Pricing Anomalies
sources.author: Andrea Frazzini, Ronen Israel, Tobias Moskowitz
project_takeaways: Any claimed edge must survive costs, turnover, impact, and capacity.
The model should prefer lower-turnover predictions around semi-annual rebalance cycles over noisy daily trading.
Backtests must report gross and net returns separately.

sources.title: Qlib: AI-oriented Quant Investment Platform
sources.author: Microsoft
project_takeaways: Use experiment tracking, dataset versioning, and reproducible pipelines.
Separate alpha model, portfolio construction, execution assumptions, and evaluation.
Future ML work should use walk-forward validation and never random splits across time.

strategy_design_rules: First replicate the public Momentum 30 rule and validate against official constituents before adding ML.
Use only point-in-time Nifty 200 membership, prices, flows, and macro/global features available at the prediction date.
Optimize for precision@30, entrant/exit hit-rate, alpha versus official Momentum 30, turnover, drawdown, and net returns after costs.
Use JEV as a robustness/overfit/leakage judge, not as an excuse to search until a lucky backtest appears.
Do not enable live trading until the model passes walk-forward tests and then paper-trades live with zero broker automation by default.
next_research_questions: Can a shadow rule predict future official Momentum 30 constituents one rebalance ahead?
Does adding global index regime improve constituent prediction or only overfit?
Do value/quality/low-vol filters reduce the historical drawdowns of pure momentum?
How much turnover and cost does an early-entry strategy add versus simply buying the official index?
